acceptanceCriteria: TestDescendantCleanupOnTimeout, TestDescendantCleanupOnCancellation and TestStdinPathDescendantCleanupOnCancellation (internal/cem/gitrun/gitrun_unix_test.go) pass 20 consecutive runs with -count=1 while another `go test ./internal/cem/...` run executes concurrently on the same host, or the test is restructured so the grandchild pid-file handshake does not depend on wall-clock deadlines under load.
The cause (missing grandchild pid file / pid not written within 30s) is diagnosed and recorded in the ticket closeout: load-induced delay versus a real cleanup defect.
body: Observed 2026-10-12 by the V1-1265 lane M builder on branch claude/v1-1265-map-schema (base 056b11643; the branch does not touch internal/cem/gitrun) while running `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=1 ./internal/cem/... ./internal/lrfrepo/... ./internal/cemcandidate/...` concurrently with two other builder lanes on the same macOS host (Darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.2). Failures: TestDescendantCleanupOnTimeout (gitrun_unix_test.go:155 open .../grandchild: no such file or directory), TestDescendantCleanupOnCancellation (gitrun_unix_test.go:194 same), TestStdinPathDescendantCleanupOnCancellation (gitrun_unix_test.go:220 pid file did not contain a parseable pid within 30s). The package passed when rerun alone immediately afterwards. Expected: the descendant cleanup proof is independent of host load. Actual: the grandchild pid-file handshake misses its deadline under concurrent go test load. Suspected flake, not a confirmed cleanup defect. Related CI flake tickets: V1-1244 (procgroup quiet proof), V1-1115.
title: gitrun descendant-cleanup tests miss the grandchild pid-file deadline under concurrent go test load (suspected flake)
